headline: Pricing and non-residential strength lift margins
summary_short: Ferguson's FY2026 Q1 revenue of $7.47B rose 3.6% y/y on price inflation and acquisitions, with diluted EPS of $2.13 up 23.1% y/y as adjusted operating profit grew 8.4% y/y to $647M.
summary_long: Revenue grew 3.6% y/y to $7.47B on price inflation and 0.8% inorganic acquisition contribution, partly offset by lower volume; U.S. non-residential sales rose ~8% on commercial/mechanical and waterworks strength while residential fell ~1% on weak construction and RMI demand. Gross margin expanded 30bp to 31.0% and SG&A leverage improved, lifting operating profit 20.7% y/y (adjusted +8.4%) to $612M. Net income rose 20.0% y/y to $414M; diluted EPS rose 23.1% to $2.13 (adjusted $2.28, +9.1%) aided by buybacks. Operating cash flow fell 11.7% y/y to $772M on higher working-capital investment. Cash was $820M against $4.1B debt; the board authorized a new $2B buyback in April 2026.

drivers.explanation: Growth driven by higher sales and associated gross profit, partially offset by higher variable operating costs; net income gain attributed to "the various elements described" in the release's line-item sections.
Mid-single-digit price inflation and 0.8% acquisition contribution, partially offset by lower volume; growth concentrated in U.S. non-residential markets.
Increased net sales and "solid execution across the business" lifted gross margin 30bp to 31.0% of sales.
Higher sales and associated gross profit, partially offset by higher variable operating costs and improved SG&A leverage.
Not separately explained beyond the combined revenue, margin, and tax-rate drivers described elsewhere in the release.
Higher net income plus the impact of share repurchases reducing diluted share count y/y.
Increased working-capital investment (receivables timing, higher inventory, vendor-payment timing), partially offset by higher net income.
Investment in new market distribution centers, the branch network, and new technology to support future growth.
